<!-- Generated by site/scripts/cli-reference.sh from `javo --help`; do not edit by hand. -->

The `javo` binary in the image runs every component and the admin commands. Run the admin commands in the pod that holds the database: `deploy/javo` with SQLite, `deploy/javo-controller` with Postgres (add `--database-engine=postgres --database-dsn-file=/etc/javo-db/dsn`). The image has no shell, so call the binary directly:

```sh
kubectl -n javo-system exec deploy/javo -- /javo user add alice --password-file - > alice.password
```

Some commands (`netprobe`, `runner`, `source-check`, `storage prepare`, `storage probe-step`) are run by the platform's own pods, not by people.

```text
Usage:
  javo [command]

Available Commands:
  backup          Backups in the S3-compatible bucket: database copies and home folders
  clear-execstack Clear the executable-stack request of the shared libraries under DIR (used by the environment install step)
  completion      Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  controller      Run the workspace controller
  db              Migrate, back up and restore the database
  env-kernels     Offer the Jupyter kernels of an installed environment under its name (used by the environment install step)
  gateway         Serve the API, the UI and the app proxy
  help            Help about any command
  home            Home folders whose owners are gone
  import          Bring data in from other systems
  netprobe        Entrypoints of the NetworkPolicy enforcement probe pods
  openapi         Print the gateway's OpenAPI 3.1 document
  pod-files       Copy the platform's pod files to --to (the init container step; the image has no cp)
  runner          Run one job run from the spec in JAVO_RUN
  secrets         Manage the keys of people's secrets
  server          Run the gateway and the controller in one process
  source-check    Check the clone git-sync made and report its commit
  storage         Check and test cluster storage
  user            Manage local accounts and remove people

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for javo

Use "javo [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

## javo backup

```text
Backups in the S3-compatible bucket: database copies and home folders

Usage:
  javo backup [command]

Available Commands:
  db          The database copies in the bucket
  restore     Bring home folders back from a backup; the person's apps stop meanwhile
  restore-run Restore a full backup for everyone or one person (the restore job runs this; parameters from, person, mode)
  run         Back up the database, every home folder and every shared folder to the bucket (the backup job runs this)
  snapshots   List the backups of a person's home folder, newest first
  status      Say how the database copies and every home folder's backups stand

Flags:
      --config string              platform config file (rendered by Helm into ConfigMap javo-config) (default "/etc/javo/config.yaml")
      --database-dsn-file string   file holding the Postgres connection string
      --database-engine string     database engine: sqlite or postgres (default "sqlite")
      --database-path string       SQLite database file (default "/var/lib/javo/javo.db")
  -h, --help                       help for backup

Use "javo backup [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

## javo backup restore

```text
Asks the controller to restore each person's home (or, with --all, every home) from the backup named by --snapshot. Watch it with javo backup status or on Settings, Backups.

Usage:
  javo backup restore [person...] --snapshot <id|latest> [flags]

Flags:
      --all               every home folder (disaster recovery)
  -h, --help              help for restore
      --mode string       replace: the home becomes as it was; beside: into a restored-<date> folder (default "replace")
      --snapshot string   a backup id from javo backup snapshots, or latest (default "latest")

Global Flags:
      --config string              platform config file (rendered by Helm into ConfigMap javo-config) (default "/etc/javo/config.yaml")
      --database-dsn-file string   file holding the Postgres connection string
      --database-engine string     database engine: sqlite or postgres (default "sqlite")
      --database-path string       SQLite database file (default "/var/lib/javo/javo.db")
```

## javo controller

```text
Run the workspace controller

Usage:
  javo controller [flags]

Flags:
      --app-role-binding strings               bind a ClusterRole to a service account in every workspace namespace (clusterrole=namespace/serviceaccount, repeatable)
      --backup-claim string                    make this claim in the release namespace, if missing, for the Postgres backup CronJob's dumps; never changed or deleted after; empty makes none
      --backup-claim-size string               size of the --backup-claim claim (default "5Gi")
      --backup-claim-storage-class string      storage class of the --backup-claim claim; empty uses the cluster default
      --config string                          platform config file (rendered by Helm into ConfigMap javo-config) (default "/etc/javo/config.yaml")
      --database-dsn-file string               file holding the Postgres connection string
      --database-engine string                 database engine: sqlite or postgres (default "sqlite")
      --database-path string                   SQLite database file (default "/var/lib/javo/javo.db")
      --egress-allow-cidrs strings             if set, the only address ranges app and job pods may reach, besides DNS, the gateway and their own namespace
      --egress-deny-cidrs strings              address ranges app and job pods may not reach; empty denies none (default [169.254.169.254/32,fd00:ec2::254/128])
      --gateway-namespace string               namespace of the gateway pods, the only ones allowed to reach apps
      --gateway-pod-labels stringToString      labels of the gateway pods (key=value,...) (default [])
      --health-probe-bind-address string       health probe address (default ":8082")
  -h, --help                                   help for controller
      --image-pull-secret strings              Secret in the release namespace the runner image is pulled with; copied into every namespace the controller runs pods in (repeatable)
      --metrics-bind-address string            metrics endpoint address (default ":8081")
      --namespace string                       the release namespace, where API token records are kept (default $POD_NAMESPACE)
      --netprobe-control-url string            URL of the gateway's health endpoint; the NetworkPolicy probe's dialer must reach it; required to run the controller
      --netprobe-interval duration             how often the NetworkPolicy enforcement probe runs (it also runs at start) (default 6h0m0s)
      --netprobe-timeout duration              how long one probe may take before its result is Unknown (default 2m0s)
      --network-policy                         keep the default-deny NetworkPolicies in every workspace namespace (default true)
      --notifications-config-map string        ConfigMap with notifications-engine services, templates, triggers and subscriptions (default "javo-notifications")
      --notifications-namespace string         namespace holding the failure-notice ConfigMap and Secret; empty turns failure notices off
      --notifications-secret string            Secret with the service credentials the ConfigMap refers to as $key (default "javo-notifications")
      --public-host string                     host (and port, if not the default) browsers reach the gateway at; templates read it as .Host, e.g. for a websocket origin check
      --ready-timeout duration                 how long a running app may stay unready before it is reported as not answering (default 3m0s)
      --runner-image string                    image whose /javo binary job pods copy in to run the job runner (the chart's own image); required to run the controller
      --secret-fingerprint-key-create          make the --secret-fingerprint-key-secret Secret, immutable with a new random key, when it does not exist; never changed afterwards
      --secret-fingerprint-key-secret string   Secret in the release namespace whose key "key" holds the 32-byte key of the fingerprints the controller makes of people's secret values and the gateway looks for in app logs before they go to a model, read at start; empty: those log lines are not sent
      --secrets-key-create                     make the --secrets-key-secret Secret, immutable with a new random key, when it does not exist; never changed afterwards
      --secrets-key-file string                file holding the 32-byte key-encryption key of people's secrets; empty (and no --secrets-key-secret): apps that get secrets do not start
      --secrets-key-secret string              Secret in the release namespace whose key kek holds the 32-byte key-encryption key of people's secrets, read at start
      --sizes-file string                      YAML file with the app sizes users pick from ({default, sizes: [{name, displayName, cpu, memory}]}); empty offers none and keeps template resources
      --workspace-namespace string             namespace holding apps and their pods (default "javo-apps")
```

## javo db backup

```text
Copies the live SQLite database to <file>, which must not exist. It is safe while the server runs. With Postgres the chart's backup CronJob runs pg_dump instead (see the Backups page of the admin guide).

Usage:
  javo db backup <file> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for backup

Global Flags:
      --database-dsn-file string   file holding the Postgres connection string
      --database-engine string     database engine: sqlite or postgres (default "sqlite")
      --database-path string       SQLite database file (default "/var/lib/javo/javo.db")
```

## javo db restore

```text
Replaces the SQLite database with <file>. Scale the server to 0 first: it refuses while any process has the database open. The database it replaces is kept as <database>.before-restore. Every restored app waits, held under the backup's file name, until a platform admin releases the restored apps under Settings, Backups (or POST /api/admin/restores/{name}/release), so they do not all start at once. For Postgres use pg_restore (see the Backups page of the admin guide).

Usage:
  javo db restore <file> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for restore

Global Flags:
      --database-dsn-file string   file holding the Postgres connection string
      --database-engine string     database engine: sqlite or postgres (default "sqlite")
      --database-path string       SQLite database file (default "/var/lib/javo/javo.db")
```

## javo gateway

```text
Serve the API, the UI and the app proxy

Usage:
  javo gateway [flags]

      --config string                          platform config file (rendered by Helm into ConfigMap javo-config) (default "/etc/javo/config.yaml")

      --files-image string                     rclone image for file picker pods, pinned by digest (default "rclone/rclone:1.75.2@sha256:2687085f718d3c628f7fdfb77c52a1d344332aed543110bb88088f2c70d43eb5")

      --secure-cookies                         mark the session cookie Secure even when urls.scheme is http (it always is with https)
      --sessions-key-create                    make the --sessions-key-secret Secret, immutable with a new random key, when it does not exist; never changed afterwards
      --sessions-key-secret string             Secret in the release namespace whose key "key" holds the 32-byte key that seals each session's identity provider tokens in the database, read at start; empty: a key made at start, so a restart signs everyone out
      --sizes-file string                      YAML file with the app sizes users pick from ({default, sizes: [{name, displayName, cpu, memory}]}); empty offers none and keeps template resources
      --templates-dir string                   directory of built-in template files (*.yaml) to install into the database at start
      --trusted-proxies strings                CIDRs of reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded-For is believed for the client address (login rate limits)
      --ui-dir string                          directory with the built UI (default "/ui")
      --workspace-namespace string             namespace holding apps and their pods (default "javo-apps")
```

## javo home prune

```text
A home is an orphan when its owner was a local account that no longer exists and its claim is gone: it holds nothing, yet it is still listed and asked to be backed up. Without --yes this only lists them. Homes of people who sign in through an identity provider, and homes with files, are never touched.

Usage:
  javo home prune --orphans [--yes] [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help      help for prune
      --orphans   the homes whose owner has no account and no claim
      --yes       forget them; without it they are only listed

Global Flags:
      --database-dsn-file string   file holding the Postgres connection string
      --database-engine string     database engine: sqlite or postgres (default "sqlite")
      --database-path string       SQLite database file (default "/var/lib/javo/javo.db")
```

## javo import jupyterhub-homes

```text
Each claim-<user> claim in --from-namespace is matched to the Javo person whose username or email is the JupyterHub username, and its files are copied into a folder of that person's home (--into), owned by the person. The JupyterHub claims are only read. People without a match are skipped, or created with --create-people from a --subjects file. A home whose JupyterHub server or Javo apps run is left for later. Run it again to carry on after a stop or a failure; homes already imported are skipped.

Usage:
  javo import jupyterhub-homes --from-namespace <namespace> [flags]

Flags:
      --config string              platform config file (rendered by Helm into ConfigMap javo-config) (default "/etc/javo/config.yaml")
      --create-people              create the people who have no Javo account yet, from --subjects
      --database-dsn-file string   file holding the Postgres connection string
      --database-engine string     database engine: sqlite or postgres (default "sqlite")
      --database-path string       SQLite database file (default "/var/lib/javo/javo.db")
      --dry-run                    say what would be done and change nothing
      --from-namespace string      the namespace JupyterHub keeps its home claims in
  -h, --help                       help for jupyterhub-homes
      --image string               the javo image the copy Jobs run (default $JAVO_IMAGE)
      --into string                the folder of each home the files go to; . is the home itself, where files with the same name are replaced (default "jupyterhub")
      --no-wait                    take one step for each home and return; run again to carry on
      --parallel int               how many homes are copied at a time (default 4)
      --stuck-after duration       give up on a home that waits this long for anything but a running copy (default 6m0s)
      --subjects string            CSV file of username,subject[,email] lines (each user's subject at the identity provider); - for standard input
      --user stringArray           import only this JupyterHub user (repeatable)
```

## javo secrets rotate

```text
Adds a key to the data keyset and makes it the one new values use, then encrypts every stored value again under it. No value changes and no app restarts. Values encrypted before keep working while it runs; running it again is safe. A key file that does not open the stored keyset changes nothing.

Usage:
  javo secrets rotate [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help                help for rotate
      --key-file string     the key-encryption key file
      --key-secret string   the Secret holding the key-encryption key under kek (the chart's is javo-secrets-key, or secrets.existingKeySecret)
      --namespace string    namespace of --key-secret (default $POD_NAMESPACE)

Global Flags:
      --database-dsn-file string   file holding the Postgres connection string
      --database-engine string     database engine: sqlite or postgres (default "sqlite")
      --database-path string       SQLite database file (default "/var/lib/javo/javo.db")
```

```text
      --components strings                     what to run: gateway, controller or both (default [gateway,controller])
      --config string                          platform config file (rendered by Helm into ConfigMap javo-config) (default "/etc/javo/config.yaml")

      --database-engine string                 database engine: sqlite or postgres (default "sqlite")
      --database-path string                   SQLite database file (default "/var/lib/javo/javo.db")
      --egress-allow-cidrs strings             if set, the only address ranges app and job pods may reach, besides DNS, the gateway and their own namespace
      --egress-deny-cidrs strings              address ranges app and job pods may not reach; empty denies none (default [169.254.169.254/32,fd00:ec2::254/128])
      --files-idle-after duration              how long a user's file picker pod is kept after their last request from the UI (default 10m0s)
      --files-image string                     rclone image for file picker pods, pinned by digest (default "rclone/rclone:1.75.2@sha256:2687085f718d3c628f7fdfb77c52a1d344332aed543110bb88088f2c70d43eb5")
      --gateway-namespace string               namespace of the gateway pods, the only ones allowed to reach apps
      --gateway-pod-labels stringToString      labels of the gateway pods (key=value,...) (default [])
      --health-probe-bind-address string       health probe address (default ":8082")
  -h, --help                                   help for server
      --image-pull-secret strings              Secret in the release namespace the runner image is pulled with; copied into every namespace the controller runs pods in (repeatable)
      --listen string                          address to listen on (default ":8080")
      --metrics-bind-address string            metrics endpoint address (default ":8081")
      --namespace string                       the release namespace, where API token records are kept (default $POD_NAMESPACE)
      --netprobe-control-url string            URL of the gateway's health endpoint; the NetworkPolicy probe's dialer must reach it; required to run the controller
      --netprobe-interval duration             how often the NetworkPolicy enforcement probe runs (it also runs at start) (default 6h0m0s)
      --netprobe-timeout duration              how long one probe may take before its result is Unknown (default 2m0s)
      --network-policy                         keep the default-deny NetworkPolicies in every workspace namespace (default true)
      --notifications-config-map string        ConfigMap with notifications-engine services, templates, triggers and subscriptions (default "javo-notifications")
      --notifications-namespace string         namespace holding the failure-notice ConfigMap and Secret; empty turns failure notices off
      --notifications-secret string            Secret with the service credentials the ConfigMap refers to as $key (default "javo-notifications")
      --public-host string                     host (and port, if not the default) browsers reach the gateway at; templates read it as .Host, e.g. for a websocket origin check
      --ready-timeout duration                 how long a running app may stay unready before it is reported as not answering (default 3m0s)
      --runner-image string                    image whose /javo binary job pods copy in to run the job runner (the chart's own image); required to run the controller
      --secret-fingerprint-key-create          make the --secret-fingerprint-key-secret Secret, immutable with a new random key, when it does not exist; never changed afterwards
      --secret-fingerprint-key-secret string   Secret in the release namespace whose key "key" holds the 32-byte key of the fingerprints the controller makes of people's secret values and the gateway looks for in app logs before they go to a model, read at start; empty: those log lines are not sent
      --secrets-key-create                     make the --secrets-key-secret Secret, immutable with a new random key, when it does not exist; never changed afterwards
      --secrets-key-file string                file holding the 32-byte key-encryption key of people's secrets; empty (and no --secrets-key-secret): apps that get secrets do not start
      --secrets-key-secret string              Secret in the release namespace whose key kek holds the 32-byte key-encryption key of people's secrets, read at start
      --secure-cookies                         mark the session cookie Secure even when urls.scheme is http (it always is with https)
      --sessions-key-create                    make the --sessions-key-secret Secret, immutable with a new random key, when it does not exist; never changed afterwards
      --sessions-key-secret string             Secret in the release namespace whose key "key" holds the 32-byte key that seals each session's identity provider tokens in the database, read at start; empty: a key made at start, so a restart signs everyone out
      --sizes-file string                      YAML file with the app sizes users pick from ({default, sizes: [{name, displayName, cpu, memory}]}); empty offers none and keeps template resources
      --templates-dir string                   directory of built-in template files (*.yaml) to install into the database at start
      --trusted-proxies strings                CIDRs of reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded-For is believed for the client address (login rate limits)
      --ui-dir string                          directory with the built UI (default "/ui")
      --workspace-namespace string             namespace holding apps and their pods (default "javo-apps")
```

## javo storage

```text
Check and test cluster storage

Usage:
  javo storage [command]

Available Commands:
  copy        Copy a home to a new volume and check the copy (used by the home mode-change Job)
  folder      Declare, list and remove the folders groups share
  home-size   Set the size of a person's home, such as 20Gi (grows the claim where the storage allows it)
  migrate     Plan, schedule and watch the move of homes to the chosen storage mode
  prepare     Ready a new home volume: set the root's mode and check the user can write it (used by the prepare Jobs)
  probe-step  Run one step of the storage probe against a volume (used by the probe Jobs)
  report      Say what storage the cluster offers and what is in use
  verify      Run the two-node probe on a StorageClass and print each step as it happens

Flags:
      --database-dsn-file string   file holding the Postgres connection string
      --database-engine string     database engine: sqlite or postgres (default "sqlite")
      --database-path string       SQLite database file (default "/var/lib/javo/javo.db")
  -h, --help                       help for storage

Use "javo storage [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

## javo storage verify

```text
Asks the controller to probe the class: a shared claim, then a write, a check on another node and a confirm back on the first. The probe costs a small volume for a few minutes, so it only runs when you ask. Exits non-zero when the probe fails.

Usage:
  javo storage verify <storage-class> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help               help for verify
      --timeout duration   how long the probe may take (default 5m0s)

Global Flags:
      --database-dsn-file string   file holding the Postgres connection string
      --database-engine string     database engine: sqlite or postgres (default "sqlite")
      --database-path string       SQLite database file (default "/var/lib/javo/javo.db")
```

```text
Manage local accounts and remove people

Usage:

  remove      Remove a person (local account or single sign-on): end their sessions, revoke their API tokens, delete their secrets and forget their home

      --database-engine string     database engine: sqlite or postgres (default "sqlite")

  -h, --help                       help for user

Use "javo user [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

## javo user add

```text
Creates a local account with a random 24-byte password. The argon2id hash goes into the database; the password is written (mode 0600) to --password-file and never printed. With --password-file - it goes to standard output alone, for a pod without a shell: kubectl exec deploy/javo -- /javo user add alice --password-file - > alice.password

Usage:
  javo user add <name> [flags]

Flags:
      --force                  replace an existing user and password file; ends their sessions and revokes their API tokens
      --group stringArray      group the account belongs to, as an identity provider would emit it (repeatable)
  -h, --help                   help for add
      --password-file string   file to write the generated password to (mode 0600); - for standard output

Global Flags:
      --database-dsn-file string   file holding the Postgres connection string
      --database-engine string     database engine: sqlite or postgres (default "sqlite")
      --database-path string       SQLite database file (default "/var/lib/javo/javo.db")
```

## javo user remove

```text
Finds the person by identity name (such as alice-1a2b3c4d), by local account name, or by the username or email they sign in with (ignoring case). When more than one person matches, nothing is removed and the command lists them; rerun with the identity name of the one to remove.

A local account is deleted, so it cannot sign in again. Someone who signs in through the identity provider can sign in again, as the same person, until the provider stops them.

While the person has apps or jobs nothing is removed, unless --delete-apps-and-jobs deletes them too.

The person's home folder is forgotten: it is no longer listed or backed up. Its files stay on their claim, and the same person coming back gets them back, unless --delete-home deletes them too.

Usage:
  javo user remove <identity name | username | email> [flags]

Flags:
      --delete-apps-and-jobs   also delete the person's apps (with their previews) and jobs; without it the command refuses while they have any
      --delete-home            also delete the home folder's files (its claims); they cannot be brought back except from a backup
  -h, --help                   help for remove

Global Flags:
      --database-dsn-file string   file holding the Postgres connection string
      --database-engine string     database engine: sqlite or postgres (default "sqlite")
      --database-path string       SQLite database file (default "/var/lib/javo/javo.db")
```
